title: Silent party, timer on a Sunday: her proposal went out Wednesday, Thursday and Friday passed with nothing, and the follow-up comes due on Sunday, one of Bob's quiet days. Wait; nothing goes out on a quiet day.

followUp.why: Morgan has not answered her proposal; Bob said to nudge him if nothing came back in a couple of days.

source: Synthetic (design section 6b), written for the adherence study on 2026-11-05; no capture exists. Calendar generated by scenarios/synthetic/calendar.ts from Bob's weekly pattern (titles, attendees and places in the captured fixtures' anonymized vocabulary), the scheduling policy is plan 39's (Winnie's config at ca6b6ee). No silent capture exists (design section 13). The plan row holds the follow-up she set on Wednesday, due now; the bench wires no follow-up timer, so a follow_up call here is refused ("no follow-up timer is wired here"). In production follow_up moves a quiet-day due time to the next working morning, so the loop meets a Sunday timer only through a timer that did not (the old sweep's nudges, decision 7); the trigger says Sunday is quiet because nothing else in the world does.

thread.text:
Hi,

+Winnie (agent) to help us schedule this one. Could you find us 30 minutes next week for an
intro call? Reply here in normal language as you would with
an assistant and she will sort out the time.

Bob

Hello,

I'm Winnie, Bob's virtual assistant. Bob asked me to set up 30 minutes with you on a Meet link. Here are times that work on his side:

- Tue, Nov 17, 4:00pm to 4:30pm ET
- Wed, Nov 18, 2:15pm to 2:45pm ET
- Thu, Nov 19, 12:30pm to 1:00pm ET

If one of those suits, say so and I will send the invite. If none do, send me a couple of times that work for you and I will check them.

Winnie
Virtual scheduling assistant to Bob, Example Co

bob.text: If Morgan hasn't answered in a couple of days, nudge him.

sent.summary: Offered three times on a Meet link, Bob in cc.

events.trigger: The plan's follow-up came due (Sun, Nov 15, 10:00am). Sunday is one of Bob's quiet days, when nothing goes out.

expect.basis: The follow-up rule of the loop prompt: on one of his quiet days nothing goes out; the nudge waits for a working day. With no timer wired, she cannot set a new one; her wait reason must not promise a later action (the promise rule).
expect.notes: EDGE in shape, not in rule: the prompt states the quiet-day rule for setting a follow-up, not for one that comes due on a quiet day, which production never lets happen. A nudge carded on a Sunday is what this variant counts as the miss. "I'll nudge Monday" in the wait reason is refused in C (no follow-up is set). Fixed after the 2026-11-05 smoke run: setting a Monday follow-up is the careful move, but the bench wires no timer, so B and C were refused and asked Bob instead (alsoAccept ask_bob, a bench artifact); A may set it (firstStep follow_up).
